case_quality_flags: Restless arms syndrome is a recognized upper-limb variant of RLS; the distinction from classic RLS is anatomical localization to arms rather than legs.
Medication contribution (escitalopram discontinuation, duloxetine increase) may have triggered or unmasked the syndrome but does not change the primary diagnosis.
Symptom persistence despite medication adjustments supports a primary sensorimotor diagnosis rather than pure withdrawal or akathisia.
